title: The Aorist Participle Active
subtitle: λύσας, λύσασα, λῦσαν — antecedent action.
objectives: Form and decline the aorist active participle of any ω-verb.
Understand the aorist participle as expressing completed action.
Use the aorist participle to show action prior to the main verb.
Distinguish aorist from present participle by meaning and form.

sections.heading: The aorist participle
sections.body:
The aorist participle expresses completed action. λύσας means 'having loosed' or 'after loosing'. The aorist participle is used for antecedent action: action that happened before the action of the main verb.

λύσας τοὺς αἰχμαλώτους ἀπῆλθεν — 'Having freed the prisoners, he went away.' The freeing happened first; the going away happened second.

The aorist participle has no augment. The augment is only for the indicative mood. The aorist participle is formed with the sigma infix (first aorist) or the strong stem (second aorist) plus participial endings.

sections.heading: The first aorist active participle: λύσας, λύσασα, λῦσαν
sections.body:
Masculine (third declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λύσας           λύσαντες
  genitive    λύσαντος        λυσάντων
  dative      λύσαντι         λύσασι(ν)
  accusative  λύσαντα         λύσαντας

Feminine (first declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λύσασα          λύσασαι
  genitive    λυσάσης         λυσασῶν
  dative      λυσάσῃ          λυσάσαις
  accusative  λύσασαν         λυσάσας

Neuter (third declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λῦσαν           λύσαντα
  genitive    λύσαντος        λυσάντων
  dative      λύσαντι         λύσασι(ν)
  accusative  λῦσαν           λύσαντα

The stem is λυσαντ-. No augment.

sections.heading: The second aorist active participle: λαβών, λαβοῦσα, λαβόν
sections.body:
Second aorist participles follow the same pattern as the present participle, but with the aorist stem.

λαβών (from λαμβάνω, aorist stem λαβ-) means 'having taken'.

              masculine       feminine        neuter
  nominative  λαβών           λαβοῦσα         λαβόν
  genitive    λαβόντος        λαβούσης        λαβόντος

The pattern is identical to λύων, λύουσα, λῦον, but with the aorist stem.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.1.2: ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπῆλθεν.
'Having said these things, he went away.' εἰπών is the aorist participle of λέγω (second aorist εἶπον). The saying happened first; the going happened second.

items.answer: genitive singular masculine or neuter of λύσας

items.prompt: What does the aorist participle express?
items.answer: Completed action, antecedent to the main verb.

items.prompt: Does the aorist participle have an augment?
items.answer: No. The augment is only for the indicative.
Having freed the prisoners, he went away.
Having said these things, he went away.

words.gloss: Having freed the prisoners, he went away.
Having taken the gift, he gave thanks.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.12 introduces the middle and passive participles. The present and aorist middle participles follow the same pattern as the active, but with middle endings. The aorist passive participle has its own forms (λυθείς), which you will learn here.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can form and decline the aorist active participle of any ω-verb and can translate aorist participles showing antecedent action.
